full_judgment:
The Rule was issued on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 22- 8-1999 passed by the Additional District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 76 of 1997 affirming those dated 22-3-1997 passed by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) should not be set aside and or any other order passed as this Court may deem fit and proper. 

 4. The plaintiff made his case in the plaint stating, inter alia, that the defendant No. 1 being the owner of the suit property started, construction of a residential building thereon in accordance with a plan approved by the DIT, but could not complete the same due to shortage of fund and thereafter entered into an agreement dated 25-2-1997 for sale of the land along with the structure standing thereon with the plaintiff at Taka 80,000. The plaintiff paid Taka 75,000 to the defendant. Ultimately, the defendant No. 1 delivered possession of the land to the plaintiff, who subsequently came to know that defendant No. 1 did not apply for income tax clearance certificate. The plaintiff had to send a notice to defendant No. 1 asking him to execute a registered sale deed but without success. Hence, the suit. 

 7. The petitioner thereafter filed Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 1995 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 23-7-1995 along with an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 74 days with the averments, inter alia, that the original suit was fixed on 5-4-1995 for further hearing in default, ex parte hearing. On 5-4-1995, the petitioner filed an application for adjournment which was allowed and the next date was fixed on 10-4-1995 for order. There was a country-wide strike (hartal) and as such, the petitioner could not attend the Court, but on his behalf: an application for adjournment was filed and the clerk of his engaged learned Advocate noted down the date in his diary as 24-6-1995. The said clerk later on came to know that the suit was already decreed on 10-4-1995. 

 8. The opposite party contested the Miscellaneous Case by filing a written objection contending, inter alia, that the case was barred by limitation. It was further contended that long 8 years after institution of the original suit, the written statement was filed on 22-11-86 and in presence of the both the parties and their learned Advocates, the case was fixed on 5-4-1995 for further hearing, in default, ex parte hearing after allowing adjournment prayer for the last time filed by the defendant No.1. On 4-5-1995, defendant No. 1 filed an adjournment prayer, which was rejected and the suit was fixed on 10-4- 1995 for order. On 10-4-1995, the ex parte decree was passed in accordance with law. 

 9. Both parties adduced evidence and the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the miscellaneous case by his judgment and order dated 22-3-1997 on the finding that the case was barred by limitation. Against this judgment and order, the petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 76 of 1997 in the Court of District Judge which Was ultimately heard by the Additional District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka who was pleased to dismiss the appeal by his judgment and order dated 22-8-1999 on the findings that the petitioner was not diligent in con- ducting his case and also on approving the finding of the trial Court. 

 11. None appears on behalf of the petitioner when the revision is taken up for hearing. It is now well settled by our Appellate Division vide the case of Safaruddin vs Fazlul Huq, 49 DLR (AD) 151 that a revision can be disposed of on merit in the absence of either party or both the parties. 

 12. Mr. Selim Reza Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos. l(a)-l(e) submits that there is no cogent and substantial ground taken in the revisional application for assailing the concurrent finding arrived at by the Courts below. He further submits that both the Courts below rightly arrived at the concurrent finding of fact that the miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was barred by limitation. He further submits that the lower appellate Court did not commit any error of law in arriving at its findings, rather the same are based on evidence on record and as such, the findings of fact arrived at by the lower appellate Court as a final Court of fact cannot be disturbed. 

 15. Admittedly, the original suit was filed on 41-1978 and the petitioner as defendant entered into appearance on 26-6-1978 and he filed his written statement on 12-11-1986 i.e. 8 years after filing of the suit. It is evident from the order sheet of the suit that the peremptory hearing of the original suit was dragged for years together mainly because of frequent adjournments taken by the present petitioner. It is further evident that at last peremptory hearing of the suit was fixed on 30-3-1995, but on that day the defendant No. 1 again filed an adjournment prayer, which was allowed giving him a last chance fixing the next date on 5-4-1995 for final hearing; in default, ex parte disposal. On 5-4-1995, the defendant again filed an adjournment prayer, which was rejected and next date was fixed on 10-4-1995 for ex parte order as the ex parte evidence was received much earlier. Thus, it appears that the defendant No. 1 dragged the hearing of the suit willfully and purposely for the reasons best known to him and it is clear that he showed his utter negligence in con- ducting his case. Such a negligent party killing valuable time of the Court without any reason whatsoever can hardly get any relief as prayed for. The lower appellate Court observed the negligence of the defendant and held that due to such negligence, the defendant was not entitled to the relief prayed for under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am also of the view that such a gross negligence on the part of the petitioner-defendant should stand in the way of getting relief under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure when the suit was rightly found to be barred by limitation. 

 16. The lower appellate Court has held that the decision taken in the case of AKM Jamaiuddin vs Mantu Lal Majumder; 49 DLR (AD) 150 as referred to on behalf of the present petitioner is not applicable in the instant case. Our Appellate Division in that case has declined to interfere with the restoration of the .suit as the suit has been restored on payment of compensatory cost to the petitioner. In the instant case, the suit was not restored on compensatory cost. Therefore, the lower appellate Court did not commit any wrong on this point. I do not find any error of law done by the lower appellate Court in dismissing the appeal resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such, the Rule does not merit consideration and the same is liable to be discharged. 

 17. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The order of stay granted in connection with the Rule stands vacated. The impugned judgment and order dated 22-8-1999 passed by the Additional District Judge, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 76 of 1997 is hereby maintained. Send down the LCR along with copies of this judgment to the Courts below immediately.
